title: A bench to wear materials down

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do you measure wear on a surface in the lab? Antoine's WearMachine repository holds the parts of a bench built for exactly that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A sample slides along a rail under a chosen load. Then it's scanned with a GelSight sensor, which captures the fine surface texture. It was used in Antoine's master's research at ÉTS on wear in texture space.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The fixtures, as CAD files. There are three families: rail parts, weight holders, and sample holders for the GelSight. The weight holders come in seven versions, from ten grams up to a kilogram, so you can set the load.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the point. STEP files let you change dimensions in a CAD tool, STL files are ready to print, and DXF outlines work for cutting flat parts. A NEMA 17 motor bracket and a lead-screw nut suggest a stepper motor drives the sliding.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is there a nice way to look at it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The written page has a 3D viewer of the printed parts, colored by family, and drawings of each one. People can rebuild the rig, adapt it, or check simulations against real measurements.
